title: Natural Deduction in Propositional Logic

definitions.definition: An expression φ₁, …, φₙ ⊢ φ meaning that φ can be formally derived from the premises φ₁, …, φₙ.
A proof system with introduction and elimination rules for each connective, designed to mirror human reasoning.
A proof system is sound if every provable sequent is also semantically valid (⊢ implies ⊨).
A proof system is complete if every semantically valid sequent is provable (⊨ implies ⊢).

formulas: ∧I: from φ and ψ derive φ ∧ ψ
→I: discharge assumption φ to derive φ → ψ from ψ
→E (modus ponens): from φ → ψ and φ derive ψ
¬I: from a proof of ⊥ under assumption φ, derive ¬φ
examples: Proof of p ∧ q ⊢ q ∧ p using ∧I and ∧E rules
Proof of p → q, p ⊢ q using →E
learning_objectives: Understand the concept of a formal proof system.
Apply natural deduction rules for propositional connectives.
Construct proof trees for given sequents.
Understand the notions of soundness and completeness.
